notes: Historical financials (revenue, operating profit/EBIT, depreciation & amortization, and capex) are taken from RTX’s FY2023–FY2025 consolidated financial statements in the FY2025 Form 10-K and converted from $ millions to full $ values. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

NWC is modeled as operating working capital: (Accounts receivable + Contract assets + Inventory + Other assets, current) − (Accounts payable + Accrued employee compensation + Other accrued liabilities + Contract liabilities), excluding cash and excluding customer financing assets. This yields negative NWC for all historical years. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))
Tax rate uses RTX’s FY2025 effective income tax rate (19.1%) as the base-case tax rate. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Cash and total debt are sourced from RTX’s FY2025 liquidity and the consolidated balance sheet (as of Dec 31, 2025); minority interest is sourced from the consolidated balance sheet. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Investments and NOL balance were not extracted into a single, clearly definable standalone input from the available extracted lines; therefore they are set to null. NOL utilization percent is modeled as 0.80 as a neutral default.

Comparable-company multiples: EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA are taken from StockAnalysis statistics pages, but the source does not explicitly label them as NTM; therefore EV/NTM fields are left null and forward P/E is populated. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/noc/statistics/))
Scenario overrides adjust only the forecast drivers (and WACC/terminal growth/target margin in the scenario assumptions) versus the base case; other historical anchors remain unchanged.

catalysts: Quarterly updates to FY2026 outlook (sales/EPS/FCF) as RTX reports operating performance and backlog execution.
Revisions to commercial aftermarket and defense production plans that could shift the sales growth trajectory and margin path.
Capital allocation updates (dividend and buybacks) supported by operating cash flow strength.
company_overview: RTX reports through three principal business segments: Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Collins Aerospace is a leading global provider of technologically advanced aerospace and defense products, with solutions including aftermarket services for civil and military aircraft manufacturers and commercial airlines. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Pratt & Whitney produces and services the PW1000G geared turbofan (GTF) engine family and sustains the F135 propulsion system for the U.S. F-35 Joint Program Office. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Raytheon delivers integrated space solutions (sensors, mission orchestration, satellite control and software) and focuses on next-generation technologies including hypersonics and advanced radars. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))
current_context: FY2025 sales were $88.6B (+10% vs. prior year; +11% organically) and free cash flow was $7.9B (operating cash flow $10.6B). ([rtx.com](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/01/27/rtx-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook))

FY2025 operating profit was $9.3B, and management reported improved profitability alongside cash generation. ([rtx.com](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/01/27/rtx-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook))

FY2026 outlook: adjusted sales of $92.0B–$93.0B with organic sales growth of 5%–6%, adjusted EPS of $6.60–$6.80, and free cash flow of $8.25B–$8.75B. ([rtx.com](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/01/27/rtx-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook))

Management cited investing in new capabilities, expanding production capacity, and executing on backlog as key drivers entering 2026. ([rtx.com](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/01/27/rtx-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook))
investment_highlights: Revenue base case (mid-single-digit growth tapering through 2030) is anchored to FY2026 organic sales guidance of 5%–6% and then converges to a more mature growth rate. ([rtx.com](https://www.rtx.com/news/news-center/2026/01/27/rtx-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook))

Base-case EBIT margin stabilizes near ~10% as historical operating profit scales from FY2023 to FY2025, reflecting continued operating leverage. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Capital intensity (capex as % of sales) declines modestly versus FY2025 levels, consistent with disciplined investment while maintaining production capacity. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))

Working-capital dynamics are modeled with negative NWC under the stated operating-working-capital definition, supporting cash conversion as sales expand. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))
key_risks: Program execution risk (schedule slips/cost growth) that can compress EBIT margin below the base-case convergence path.
Geopolitical and defense-spending uncertainty, including procurement timing changes across U.S. and international customers.
Manufacturing/supply chain and technology transition risks (including engine/production quality and advanced system development delays).

presentation.subtitle: RTX (RTX) DCF Input Package — FY2023-2025 History; FY2026-2030 Base/Bull/Bear
valuation_summary: DCF inputs are anchored to RTX’s FY2023–FY2025 GAAP revenue, operating profit (EBIT), D&A, and capex from its Form 10-K, with conservative normalization of margins and reinvestment over FY2026–FY2030. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000101829/000130817926000038/rtx014050-ars.pdf))
Terminal value uses a Gordon growth approach with economically conservative long-run growth (2.0%) and a base WACC (8.4%).

Peer comps act as a valuation plausibility check using EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA-style multiples and forward P/E from StockAnalysis. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/noc/statistics/))
